_meta.indication: POTELIGEO is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory mycosis fungoides (MF) or Sezary syndrome (SS) after at least one prior systemic therapy.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, open-label, randomized, actively controlled phase 3 trial randomizing 1:1 to mogamulizumab vs vorinostat until progression, with one-way crossover.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with mycosis fungoides (MF) or Sezary syndrome (SS) after at least one prior systemic therapy (median = 3).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS-INV).
pivotal_trials.result: Investigator-assessed median PFS 7.6 months (95% CI 5.6, 10.2) with mogamulizumab vs 3.1 months (95% CI 2.8, 4.0) with vorinostat; HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.41, 0.69; p<0.0001). Confirmed ORR per investigator 28% vs 5% (p<0.0001).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) were rash, infusion related reactions, fatigue, diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, and upper respiratory tract infection. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 36% (66/184), most often infection (16%). Fatal adverse reactions within 90 days occurred in 2.2% (7/319). Fatal and life-threatening skin reactions including SJS and TEN, and immune-mediated complications, have occurred.
target_moa: Mogamulizumab is a defucosylated, humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that selectively binds CC chemokine receptor 4 (CCR4), which is overexpressed on T-cell malignancy cells, targeting CCR4-expressing cells for lysis by antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC).
modality: mAb (defucosylated humanized IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody).

rems.type: The clinical review team did not recommend a REMS; safety issues can be adequately managed through labeling and routine post-marketing surveillance.

companion_dx_detail: A companion diagnostic for CCR4 expression was determined not to be required for safe and effective use of mogamulizumab.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the biologic in treatment of the disease.

basis.text: Granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation in 8/2017 for treatment of MF or SS after at least one prior systemic therapy, based on top-line results from randomized phase 3 trial 0761-010.

citations.quote: Based on top-line results from a randomized phase 3 trial (0761-010), mogamulizumab was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation in 8/2017 for the treatment of MF or SS after at least one prior systemic therapy.

orphan_indication.text: Granted Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of CTCL in 11/2010.

citations.quote: Mogamulizumab was granted Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of CTCL in 11/2010.

summary.text: Mogamulizumab-kpkc received Orphan Drug Designation (11/2010) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (8/2017) for MF or SS; the BLA was granted Priority review and received regular (non-accelerated) approval based on the randomized phase 3 trial 0761-010.

citations.quote: Mogamulizumab was granted Orphan Drug Designation for the treatment of CTCL in 11/2010. Based on top-line results from a randomized phase 3 trial (0761-010), mogamulizumab was granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation in 8/2017 for the treatment of MF or SS after at least one prior systemic therapy.

This review team recommends regular approval of mogamulizumab (POTELIGEO) for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory mycosis fungoides (MF) or Sézary syndrome (SS) after at least one prior systemic therapy.

requirement.text: PMR 3459-1: Characterize complications after allogeneic HSCT following mogamulizumab-kpkc in at least 50 patients with hematologic malignancies (at least 40 with CTCL), of whom at least two-thirds received mogamulizumab as the last regimen prior to HSCT; evaluate toxicities at least through transplant Day 180.
